items.title: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
items.detailText:
Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, our new models for the hardest technical challenges. Fable 5.2 sets a new bar in coding, finance, and the sciences.
We’ve upgraded Claude Fable and Claude Mythos—models that are designed to tackle the most daunting technical challenges.
Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 show improvements in areas like coding, reasoning, and vision. During prerelease testing they’ve helped our engineers complete otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes, made substantial progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours—among many other applications we’ll discuss below.
Claude Fable and Claude Mythos are the same underlying model. Fable has strong cybersecurity and biology safeguards to guard against misuse, which allows us to make it available to all users. Organizations pursuing beneficial applications in cybersecurity or biomedical research can apply for access to Mythos through our recently expanded Life Sciences and Cyber Verification Programs.
Testers have found that Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 communicate more clearly than past Fable and Mythos models. They generate outputs up to 30% faster than Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, and they’re available at a lower price: $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens.
Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 also come with an optional fast mode, which speeds up token generation by up to 2.5 times. Fast mode is available for $16 per million input tokens and $80 per million output tokens.
We describe more about our safety testing below, and full details can be found in the Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 System Card .

For details on evaluation methodology, see the Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 System Card . All scores show each model’s highest-available effort unless otherwise noted. † On CyScenarioBench, each lab’s scores are based on unique tasks. ‡ RoboDojo Sim shows the highest-available effort and was run internally.
Effort and efficiency. On Medium effort (the default in Claude apps and Claude Code), Fable 5.2 can accomplish challenging tasks with fewer tokens than Fable 5.1. In early testing on the FrontierCode 2.0 evaluation, Fable 5.2 at High effort scored about level with Opus 5.5 at Max effort, for roughly half the cost per task. At Xhigh effort, it also scored the highest of any released model tested.

items.title: Introducing Muse Spark 1.1
items.detailText:
Today, we’re excited to introduce Muse Spark 1.1, the latest model from Meta Superintelligence Labs and a significant upgrade from Muse Spark. Muse Spark 1.1 is a multimodal reasoning model built for agentic tasks, with major gains in tool and computer use, coding, and multimodal understanding.
With these improvements, Muse Spark 1.1 advances the performance-efficiency frontier. Together with this week’s launch of Muse Image , this release brings us closer to our vision of personal superintelligence: models that help you pursue your goals, create what you imagine, deepen your relationships, and take action on what you value most.
Along with this release, we are launching a public preview of the new Meta Model API where developers can access Muse Spark 1.1. The model is available now in "Thinking" mode in the Meta AI app and on meta.ai .
For more details about our evaluations, see our report .
Muse Spark 1.1 delivers exceptional performance in personal agentic tasks that require planning and orchestration across a range of external apps and services. It zero-shot generalizes to new native tools, MCP servers, and custom skills.
It tackles complex projects significantly faster than Muse Spark, as it is trained to orchestrate multi-agent systems to optimize end-to-end latency. As the main agent, it can gather context, make a plan, and delegate execution across parallel subagents. As a subagent, it adheres to its job, understands available tools, and knows when to escalate back to the main agent.
Muse Spark 1.1 can actively manage its context window of 1 million tokens. It remembers actions, retrieves information from much earlier work, and compacts in a way that keeps the critical steps needed for later work.
Muse Spark 1.1 excels at computer-use workflows that unfold across multiple applications with information changing on-the-fly. It maintains context across extended sessions, adapts to evolving requirements, and navigates unfamiliar interfaces with minimal human intervention.
Rather than reasoning through every desktop step one click at a time, Muse Spark 1.1 understands when to automate and when to use the interface directly. We trained the model to write scripts when automation is faster, click when direct interaction is simpler, and generate batches of actions at each step.
Agentic dinner party organization: In real-world applications, new context arises that changes the task. Muse Spark 1.1 notices these changes when placing the dinner order and makes necessary updates without user intervention.

items.title: Introducing Muse Image and Muse Video
items.detailText:
Muse Image follows instructions faithfully, edits with precision, composes from multiple references, and draws on Instagram for social context. Muse...
We’re excited to launch Muse Image and preview Muse Video, the first media generation models developed by Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Image is our most advanced image generation model yet: it follows instructions faithfully, edits with precision, and composes from multiple references. It also brings agentic tool use capabilities and integrates with Muse Spark. Muse Video, built on the same pretraining base, delivers exceptional visual fidelity with native audio support.
Muse Image is available today across the Meta AI app and on meta.ai , Instagram Stories in the US, and WhatsApp in limited countries, and is coming soon to Facebook. Muse Video is coming soon to creators and Meta AI.
Instead of directly mapping prompts to images, Muse Image operates as an agent: it invokes search and coding tools to improve accuracy, self-refines its own generations, and improves through scaling test-time compute. Muse Image also integrates with Muse Spark, allowing the two models to share tools and plan jointly for powerful agentic media generation.
We provide Muse Image with access to tools to enhance its agentic capabilities.
Coding. During reinforcement learning, Muse Image learns to write and execute code that produces accurate plots and QR codes, and condition on rendered figures to improve the accuracy of generated images. Muse Spark and Muse Image also integrate to use the combination of code and media generation to create animated GIFs, websites with embedded images, and interactive visual games.
Search. Muse Image learns to search the web to ground generated images in factual and real-time information and visual references. Enabling search improves factual accuracy on knowledge-intensive prompts, particularly those involving current events and real-world facts.
Muse Image improves with search tool use. Win rate from internal ablation.
Muse Image reflects on and improves upon its own work within its chain of thought. This self-refining behavior can take different forms: a local edit to the current image draft when a small detail is off, a new image generation from scratch when larger parts are wrong, or a different tactic like tool use for more factually accurate generation. We didn’t design this behavior. Instead, it emerged during RL training simply because self-refinement produced better images and therefore higher reward.
Muse Image improves with emergent self-refinement. Win rate from internal ablation.

items.title: AI服务的使用量持续增长，正在吸引一批原本分属不同行业的企业进入同一条生意链。
items.detailText:
AI服务的使用量持续增长，正在吸引一批原本分属不同行业的企业进入同一条生意链。
AI服务的使用量持续增长，正在吸引一批原本分属不同行业的企业进入同一条生意链。能源企业向算力运营延伸，云厂商重新组织模型与应用业务，设备企业增加推理部署方案，电商平台开始销售AI服务。围绕Token形成的市场，已经超出了大模型公司的经营范围。
需求的变化有一个直观刻度。国家数据局网站10月刊发的一篇专家解读援引相关统计：截至2026年6月，我国日均词元调用量已超过500万亿。更多任务持续调用模型，也让部署、交付、计费和分发，成为可以独立组织的业务。
过去讨论AI商业化，注意力更多集中在模型能力、应用产品和用户规模。如今，越来越多企业开始计算另一笔账：持续发生的AI调用，会消耗多少电力和设备能力，需要怎样的运营服务，又能通过什么渠道卖给客户。
Token把这些原本分散的环节连接了起来。它是模型处理信息的计量单位，也被用于描述一部分AI服务的消耗与收费。各行业争取的，是这笔持续支出的不同部分。能否把原有资源变成稳定收入，将决定这场跨界的成色。
今年3月，阿里巴巴成立Alibaba Token Hub事业群，将创造、交付与应用Token作为组织方向，并把模型即服务，也就是MaaS，放到更重要的位置。基础模型、服务平台和应用被放在同一套业务安排中，目标是让模型被更多任务持续使用。
这类调整反映了一种经营上的延伸：模型训练完成以后，长期运行、适配和服务客户，本身就是另一项工作。企业客户要把模型接进业务，除了比较能力，还要处理部署方式、访问权限、服务稳定性、用量和费用。围绕这些需求提供服务，可以形成与训练基础模型不同的分工。
跨境市场进一步扩大了这种分工。青岛自贸片区与浪潮云8月签署合作协议，共建跨境词元工厂，将异构算力、多类模型接入、计量计价和跨境结算放到一个服务平台中。9月，相关项目完成了面向韩国客户的内容生成业务验证，中国联通承担国际传输通道，词元工厂组织算力与模型处理。
这里交付的已经是一段完整服务：客户提出需求，数据经过网络传输，模型完成处理，结果再交到客户手里。模型只是其中一个关键环节，网络、部署、支付与服务支持，都有明确的位置。计算设备可以留在本地，服务则有机会面向更广的客户。
这也解释了为什么一家公司即使没有自研基础大模型，仍然有参与的机会。成熟模型可以被调用或部署，缺少稳定算力、行业适配、客户渠道或者运营支持，同样会影响使用。原来积累在其他业务里的能力，可以在这些环节找到新的付费对象。
但从按台、按机时提供资源，走到按调用提供模型服务，交付责任会增加。设备能否启动只是起点，模型运行速度、并发承载和服务中断，都会直接影响客户业务。原有资源可以降低入场成本，持续交付仍然需要新的技术和运营能力。
协鑫能科已经提出向Token交易服务商转型，服务范围包括空间、异构算力租赁和定制智算方案。原有能源资产和调度经验，成为它向计算服务延伸的基础。对这类企业而言，卖电之外增加部署与运营服务，有机会参与更长的收入链条。
不过，一度电的价格与一次模型服务的成本，中间隔着设备利用率、推理效率、网络和运维。电便宜，只有在设备持续处理有效任务时，才能变成有意义的成本优势。空闲设备同样占用资金，客户也不会为尚未交付的计算能力付款。
11月5日的采访中，英特尔中国区董事长王稚聪谈到绿色算力舱的设想：在绿电资源附近部署计算设备，再与算力运营和调度企业合作，把分布式资源组织起来。他把这一过程概括为，在发电场所将绿电转化成Token。
这份设想中，储能、配电和散热占据了重要位置。风电、光伏的供给会波动，计算任务也有自己的负载节奏，二者需要通过系统衔接。储能用于缓冲供电与负载变化，配电、计算模块和散热系统则共同决定设备能否稳定工作。
王稚聪介绍，相关架构协同花了约三个季度，涉及数十家合作伙伴。有限空间里，液冷管件、供电方式、储能模块与机柜都要匹配，不同供应商的产品必须能够连接和扩展。把设备装进一个舱体，背后是多个行业共同完成的系统工程。
这段过程说明，传统企业进入AI服务，并不只是给原有资产换一个名字。能源企业要补计算运营，设备企业要配合供电和散热，算力运营商要接上网络、模型与客户。谁能把这些环节组织好，谁才有条件将资源优势传递到服务价格和可靠性上。
英特尔在这套合作里仍然定位于基础技术研发与供应商，不以自己的品牌直接向最终用户销售算力舱。王稚聪当时预计，项目可能在2027年上半年开始落地。芯片、能源和运营企业参与的是同一类需求，取得收入的方式和承担的责任却各不相同。
部署位置也因此不能只按电价决定。适合远端处理的任务，有机会利用更好的能源条件；对响应速度、数据管理或现场协同有要求的企业，则可能选择就近部署。客户愿意支付的，是符合业务条件的服务。便宜的电是其中一个要素，完整交付才是商品。
游族网络全资子公司近日签署42.25亿元GPU采购合同，计划组合使用自有资金、银行授信和金融租赁，设备分批交付。采购方先支付预付款，再按约定支付批次尾款，交付时间还受到原厂和上级供应商安排的影响。
这份合同明确了设备采购，后续业务组织方式尚未完整公开。设备销售、算力租赁与模型服务，对应的是三套不同的经营要求：销售关心交付与回款，租赁需要承担部署、运维和利用率，模型服务还要继续负责软件适配、调用管理和客户支持。
这种区别会影响资金怎样收回来。采购设备花出去的是一笔大额投入，租赁和调用收入则要在使用中逐步形成。客户需求不足，设备仍会占用资金；技术与服务价格变化，又会改变收入预期。企业需要协调设备到货、客户上线和回款三个节奏。
科技日报10月报道的广州腾元数字，向上游预付算力词元、模型授权和流量费用，下游客户却有较长回款周期。业务增长带来了更大的资金缺口，公司随后取得300万元、期限3年的纯信用“词元贷”。
游族的合同首先锁定设备采购义务，下游客户、用途和收入尚未披露；腾元则是在服务已经卖出以后，遇到上游预付与下游回款不同步。一个要让大额设备投入得到持续使用，一个要为正在增长的业务垫付成本。原有的资本、客户与授信能力，分别决定企业能承受多长的等待。
银行对这类业务的判断也在变化。相关授信除了参考词元消耗，还会考察结算周期、使用效率、历史财务和回款等信息。调用记录能够反映业务活动，最终偿还资金仍然要靠有效收入。
Token生意由此形成了新的筛选条件：设备数量决定一部分承载能力，客户结构影响负载，运营能力影响交付成本，资金安排决定企业能否撑过投入与回款之间的间隔。原来行业里的“家底”，要经过这些具体环节才能发挥作用。

items.title: 机器人进校园，关键在课程和开发生态。
items.detailText:
机器人进校园，关键在课程和开发生态。
近日，在第88届中国教育装备展示会上，地瓜机器人与宇树科技首次联合参展，并宣布达成深度合作，联合推出面向中小学的具身智能教育解决方案。
此次合作以地瓜机器人旭日S100智能计算平台为核心算力底座，结合宇树科技Go2四足机器人、R1人形机器人，以及古月居桌面机器人等硬件， 配套15款主题课程、共180节课，覆盖小学、初中和高中三个学段。
同时，双方还将提供课赛融合实践项目、教材资源及教学环境建设，试图为学校提供从机器人硬件到课程内容的一体化解决方案。
这次合作的分工比较明确：宇树提供机器人本体，地瓜提供算力平台和开发生态。双方希望将机器人硬件、底层计算能力与教学内容整合起来，让学生不仅能看到机器人运动， 还能进一步理解和参与机器人的感知、计算、控制等开发过程。
值得注意的是，这也是地瓜机器人教育业务的一次延伸。此前，地瓜的教育合作主要集中在高校和开发者生态，如今开始向中小学课程与教学解决方案拓展。
宇树科技则在今年7月与成都市锦江区共建基础教育具身智能实验室，此次合作进一步丰富了其面向中小学的产品和课程体系。
对机器人企业而言，教育正在成为具身智能落地的新场景。 与工业、商业等场景相比，学校对机器人运动能力和生产效率的要求并不完全相同，但对设备的可操作性、教学内容和长期使用价值有着自己的要求。
如何让一台机器人从展示设备变成真正的教学工具，成为各家具身智能公司需要回答的问题。
如果一台机器人只是出现在校园开放日、科技节或者实验室展台上，完成几次行走、舞蹈和互动表演，那么它的教育价值有限。 只有当学生能够围绕机器人持续编程、调试、完成任务，并在过程中理解感知、决策和运动控制等技术，硬件才真正成为教学工具。
这也是地瓜与宇树此次合作值得关注的地方。 180节课程、课赛融合项目和真机开发 ，意味着双方希望将机器人变为可供学生持续学习和开发的教学工具。
宇树的优势在于四足机器人和人形机器人的本体研发、运动控制及整机产品能力。但机器人要进入课堂，仅有一台性能不错的机器还不够。学校还需要适合学生上手的开发工具、稳定的计算平台，以及与不同年龄段相匹配的课程内容。 地瓜提供的，正是这套基础设施中的一部分。
在技术层面，旭日S100智能计算平台在单颗SoC内集成CPU、BPU与MCU，将机器人感知决策与实时运动控制整合在同一平台，为机器人提供端侧计算支持。
对于学生而言，这意味着他们可以从观察机器人执行任务，进一步进入感知、计算和控制等环节，开展真实设备上的开发实践。
双方还按照不同学段设计了从桌面级机器人到四足、人形机器人的进阶实践路径，并设置双机器人接力、Go2稳定运输挑战、R1机器人裁判等课赛融合项目。 这类任务能够给学生提供相对具体的学习目标，也更容易将课程、社团活动和赛事连接起来。
宇树科技普教事业部负责人姜永胜表示， 让机器人在学校里持续用起来，需要计算平台、开发工具和教学资源共同配合。 地瓜机器人旭日S100的端侧计算能力，加上配套课程和教育生态资源，有助于宇树将本体能力转化为更完整的教学方案。期待双方在教育实践中打磨产品，也共同发掘更多行业的应用需求。
地瓜机器人生态副总裁胡春旭则表示，宇树在核心零部件、运动控制和整机产品上的研发实力，与地瓜机器人智能计算平台形成了良好互补。高性能的四足、人形本体，将为地瓜计算平台带来更丰富的开发场景，教育是双方长期协作的起点，希望共同支持开发者成长，并在更多产品上实现本体与计算平台的深度协同。
从这次合作看，双方正尝试降低学校开展具身智能教育的门槛。 对于缺乏机器人开发经验的学校来说，硬件、开发平台、课程和教学资源能够一并提供，显然比单独采购设备更容易形成实际教学。
据了解，教育是地瓜与宇树此次合作的首个落地场景，双方未来还计划向工业等更多领域拓展。
此前，各家具身智能公司教育市场主要是面向高校科研和开发者，如今不少公司开始进一步向中小学延伸。
地瓜机器人于2024年1月成立，由地平线机器人事业部拆分而来，主要为机器人行业提供软硬件通用底座与开发基础设施。
2026年4月，地瓜机器人完成1.5亿美元B2轮融资，B轮累计融资达到2.7亿美元。
自2023年起，地瓜机器人便与多所高校开展合作，共建机器人专业及人才培养体系。通过DUP高校开发者计划， 地瓜机器人已与500余所高校建立合作，累计开展课程与活动超过1000场，并聚合50余家教育伙伴。
这次和宇树合作，则是进入中小学。这一变化也反映出地瓜机器人的思路：高校侧重开发者培养和技术研究，中小学则更需要适合不同年龄段的课程、标准化教学工具和教师支持。 前者帮助企业建立技术开发者生态，后者则有机会扩大具身智能技术的普及范围。
宇树科技也在推进类似的拓展，教育是其商业的起点。 2026年三季度报告中没有单独披露宇树人形机器人的收入结构，根据此前招股书披露的数据， 2025年前三季度，宇树人形机器人收入中有73.60%来自科研教育，高度依赖高校、科研院所和开发者的采购。而今，宇树科技拓展到中小学。
今年7月24日，宇树与成都市锦江区共建的宇树科技·成都锦江（嘉祥）具身智能实验室在嘉祥外国语学校揭牌。这是宇树首个面向基础教育阶段的具身智能实训平台，涉及人形机器人实训、四足机器人实践、动作捕捉、遥控操控以及配套课程和教学资源。
此次与地瓜合作， 则进一步将机器人本体、计算平台和课程体系整合起来。对宇树而言，除了通过区域合作进入学校，也开始借助产业伙伴补齐教学开发生态。
事实上，优必选早已在这一市场积累多年经验。作为上一轮机器人产业化的代表，优必选在2016年前后便开始布局教育业务，逐渐形成涵盖教育机器人、AI课程、教师培训和赛事活动的业务体系。 它是较早将机器人带入中小学的企业之一，也经历了机器人教育从硬件销售向整体解决方案发展的过程。
过去，优必选主要是把机器人带进课堂，让学生学习机器人和人工智能；现在，它也开始尝试让机器人本身成为课堂里的教学工具。
例如，在基础教育领域，优必选推出的Walker C1 EDU Tutor搭载UIRO优诺智能助教系统，可完成自主授课、拍题讲解、智能问答和多模态课堂互动等工作，试图为学校提供一体化智能助教解决方案。
不过，优必选近两年也在大力拓展制造、仓储等工业场景，教育业务也面临经营压力。根据优必选2026年中期财报，上半年公司来自其他智能机器人产品及解决方案的收入同比下降18.8%至约2.46亿元， 主要由于教育智能机器人及智能机器人解决方案收入减少。
加速进化选择了一个相对具体的入口：机器人足球。它试图以赛事带动教学，以教学推动机器人普及，再通过开发者生态形成持续的用户连接。 据加速进化今年9月披露，北京已有30多所中学使用其工具开设具身智能课程。

items.title: Anthropic豪掷34亿美元直采发电设备保AI算力供电
items.detailText:
Anthropic豪掷34亿美元直采发电设备保AI算力供电
据日前媒体报道，Anthropic 9月下旬与燃气发电设备供应商OnePWR Solutions达成一笔大规模交易，为数据中心采购燃气发电机组。
这次交易金额高达34亿美元，包括总装机容量达1.7GW的重型发电机组，以及安装这些发电机组所需的工程设计及施工部分。
在此之前，AI公司通常依赖公用事业公司或专业电力公司来满足电力需求，但如今随着燃气轮机与发电机组需求激增，设备制造的交付周期已拉长至数年，而AI公司开始利用自身雄厚的资金实力绕过中间商，直接切入设备环节。
值得注意的是， Anthropic本次交易并非直接向OnePWR单纯购买设备，也不是收购OnePWR。
知情人士透露，OnePWR在两年前就向设备制造商卡特彼勒（Caterpillar）订购了发电机组，但由于其缺乏资金导致无法完成这笔交易。Anthropic原计划成为OnePWR的客户，但之后决定直接接手OnePWR向卡特彼勒订购的这笔设备订单，
借由这笔交易， Anthropic获得了两年前就已下单的发电机组，可以说这笔交易在价格与交期上具备双重优势：订购时间在价格大幅上涨之前，且Anthropic在近期及未来两年内就能获得设备供应。
Anthropic几天前透露，截至2045年，公司已承诺的算力采购及相关安排总额接近9000亿美元，此前其高度依赖外部来保障电力、芯片、数据中心与土地等资源，并需要支付溢价锁定产能。直接采购发电机组，则能让Anthropic更好地掌控电力供应。
Stifel董事总经理兼清洁能源与电力业务主管Arash Nazhad表示，从企业角度看，如果能拥有部分电力基础设施，并把这种能力掌控在手上，就能更好地保护自己，降低外部因素干扰风险。
站在当前时点，电力依旧是科技巨头数据中心扩张的一项关键桎梏。 微软近期因电力供应问题导致项目投入使用时间延迟，退出了一项数据中心租赁承诺；甲骨文位于美国新墨西哥州的项目也面临电力供应审批困难。
本月初，高盛在研报中大幅上调全球数据中心容量预测，预计到2030年全球数据中心容量将达273GW，较此前预测的217GW增幅达26%。其指出，随着数据中心建设规模扩大，项目能否获得可靠电力供应，正在成为决定建设进度的重要条件。

items.title: Kitta: Code Review Agent for Higher-Quality Code Reviews
items.description: Kitta: Code Review Agent for Higher-Quality Code Reviews This article introduces Kitta, a domain-customized Code Review Agent that leverages project-specific knowledge and tailored workflows to deliver expert-level code reviews. Alibaba Clo
items.detailText:
This article introduces Kitta, a domain-customized Code Review Agent that leverages project-specific knowledge and tailored workflows to deliver expert-level code reviews.
This article is excerpted from the Alibaba Cloud AI Agent Handbook . Project URL: https://github.com/aliyun/ai-agent-handbook
Now that AI-assisted programming has become widespread, code output has grown exponentially while review capacity has not kept pace. For foundational software such as kernels, PR size and review time have both surged; general-purpose AI review tools, lacking domain knowledge and an understanding of the business, cannot meet expert-level review requirements. The bottleneck in R&D efficiency is shifting rapidly from "writing" to "reviewing."
This article introduces Kitta, a Code Review Agent deeply customized for a specific domain. It turns a general-purpose agent into a domain specialist: by accumulating project-level expert assets, customizing the review workflow and the domain knowledge base, and building a closed loop of coordinated online and offline evolution, it precisely addresses domain-specific code issues.
Let us start with a few sets of numbers.
The data on R&D efficiency points to the same trend. DORA (the R&D-efficiency research program under Google Cloud) reports in its annual study State of AI-assisted Software Development that while AI takes part in development more deeply, the code bug rate rises by 9%, code review time by 91%, and average PR size by 154% (this edition surveyed about 5,000 respondents, and the figures are a correlation measure rather than a causal conclusion).
In short, in an era of human-AI co-authored coding, writing code is no longer limited by human capacity, but review capacity has not grown along with it. The productivity bottleneck is moving from "writing" to "reviewing."
Facing this trend, the OpenAnolis community is exploring what an AI Native R&D organization looks like, and is upgrading continuous integration into Agentic Continuous Integration. The pipeline has four stages:
It is clear that AI review sits in a position that connects what comes before with what follows: upstream, AI-assisted programming pushes the volume of code output up, and downstream, intelligent testing and community merging both rest on the premise that the code entering those stages is sound. If the review stage gives way, defects either leak downstream or Maintainers are overwhelmed by the flood of PRs produced by human-AI co-authoring. This is the problem Kitta is meant to solve.

items.title: Reliably Reproducing Over 70% of Defects: An Agent Pipeline from Alerts to Automated Fixes in Practice
items.description: Reliably Reproducing Over 70% of Defects: An Agent Pipeline from Alerts to Automated Fixes in Practice This article introduces an AI Agent pipeline that autonomously investigates, reliably reproduces, and fixes software defects from alerts
items.detailText:
This article introduces an AI Agent pipeline that autonomously investigates, reliably reproduces, and fixes software defects from alerts to streamline developer workflows.
Project URL: https://github.com/aliyun/ai-agent-handbook
This article is excerpted from the practical chapters of the open-source project Alibaba Cloud AI Agent Handbook. The project has also launched a mini-game with Agent engineering challenges. You are welcome to try it.
At the beginning of the year, I fixed a bug that left a deep impression on me. In the end, only two lines of code actually needed changing, but checking logs, reviewing monitoring data, and analyzing the issue beforehand took me an entire day. To reproduce the issue, I had to squeeze in repeated debugging sessions between meetings, and it took nearly a week in total to finish. After that, I still had to add test cases and follow up on code review until the code was merged.
AI can already help us write code. But if it only helps me write those two lines, it does not really save much time. Could we also hand over the work that actually consumes all that time?
This article shares some engineering practices from PolarDB-X team: enabling an Agent to start with an alert or a ticket, autonomously investigate, reproduce, fix, and validate the issue, and then hand the results over to developers for review.
PolarDB-X is a distributed database. Databases support the business operations of many users. When something goes wrong, it can disrupt those operations or even cause data corruption. We therefore have very high requirements for correctness and reliability.
Distributed systems are also inherently complex. They have multiple components and modules, and multiple versions may coexist in production. A change in one place can affect other functionality, making coding, troubleshooting, and regression validation more difficult. Involving an Agent in development requires meeting these same requirements.
After a period of practical experience, we divided development tasks into two categories and adopted different collaboration approaches for each.
The first category is developing new features or iteratively optimizing existing ones, such as optimizing distributed transactions or implementing new data compression capabilities. These tasks involve more components, and many implementation details need ongoing adjustment during development. Developers still need to lead solution design and key decisions, while the Agent mainly assists with coding and testing.

items.description: The Future of AI: from Enterprise Adoption to Open Source Sovereignty
items.detailText:
In this episode, a panel of AI experts, Meryem Arik (DoubleWord), Clara Higuera Cabañes (BBVA), and Jeff Smith (C Proof), demystify the current state of AI in the enterprise.
A monthly overview of things you need to know as an architect or aspiring architect.
Facilitating the Spread of Knowledge and Innovation in Professional Software Development
Unlock the full InfoQ experience by logging in! Stay updated with your favorite authors and topics, engage with content, and download exclusive resources.
Lily Mara explains how to avoid high-risk software rewrites through incremental FFI refactoring. She shares how engineering teams can replace Python bottlenecks with Rust via PyO3, demonstrating how to achieve dramatic function-level speedups, seamless integration testing, and meaningful infrastructure cost savings without microservice overhead.
Agentic AI architecture extends microservices and cloud-native architectures with AI agents that work with context, memory, and protocols such as MCP and A2A. The article covers bounded-context integration, task-dependent coordination strategies, new security risks, and observability needs. It expects gradual adoption alongside existing architectures, with platforms absorbing common components.
In this episode, Edoardo Vacchi discusses the evolving landscape of WebAssembly on the backend, running Java workloads on GPUs using TornadoVM, and optimizing distributed AI inference using llm-d and vLLM on Kubernetes. Edoardo explains how llm-d manages cache locality (KV and prefix caches), request routing, and batch inference across Kubernetes clusters to maximize expensive GPU utilization.
Vanessa Formicola shares how technical leaders can move beyond "wishful architecture" by practicing holistic socio-technical engineering. She discusses why engineering leaders must account for organizational maturity, reward structures, geopolitical climate, and team dynamics, framing the staff-plus role as designing the conditions for technology to thrive rather than just picking tools.
Colin Douch shares battle-tested strategies for building and scaling self-hosted observability stacks. He explains how to effectively correlate metrics, structured logs, and distributed traces using open-source tooling like Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics, and Jaeger, while navigating the engineering trade-offs of avoiding SaaS vendor lock-in.

items.title: Donating Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
items.detailText:
Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.
Today, we’re donating Agent Skills , the open standard that gives AI agents specialized knowledge and workflows, to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF). More than 70 agent platforms, including ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and VS Code, have integrated Agent Skills since we published the standard in December 2025.
We’re committed to keeping Agent Skills open, community-driven, and vendor-neutral. Today, we are donating the standard to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation, which we co-founded with Block and OpenAI last year, and to which we donated the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The AAIF will provide a neutral home to the standard going forward, ensuring the community has a say in where Agent Skills go next.
We are donating the Agent Skills name and logo, the GitHub organization, and the agentskills.io domain. You can continue to use the standard or contribute to it without joining the AAIF.
Engineers from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, and other companies will maintain the standard as individuals, with David Soria Parra and Mahesh Murag as Lead Maintainers.
We’ve proposed starting with a roadmap covering versioned releases, a formal proposal process, and security guidance for people who write and install skills. As with MCP, the project will continue to prioritize community input and transparent decision-making. You can join the project’s Discord to give feedback on proposed specification changes.
Thank you to the developers who built with Agent Skills from the start, and to the teams who brought skills into their products. Read the specification at agentskills.io and join the discussion on GitHub .
Anthropic is a Public Benefit Corporation. Our mission is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.

items.title: AI Guardrails Checklist: 7 Controls Every Enterprise Deployment Needs on Day One
items.description: AI Guardrails Checklist: 7 Controls Every Enterprise Deployment Needs on Day One Guardrails are not distrust. They are what make a production launch signable. In this guide, we will discuss seven runtime guardrails, placed in the order a re
items.detailText:
Guardrails are not distrust. They are what make a production launch signable. In this guide, we will discuss seven runtime guardrails, placed in the order a request meets them.
Only 5% of companies have the full set of controls in place for agentic AI (BCG, Applied AI Index 2026, 2026). Many still launch with one guardrail: the model's own judgment. A model-based check on every request can cost under 3% of the model bill. Skipping it is the expensive choice.
Guardrails are not distrust. They are what make a production launch signable.
Agent adoption is moving faster than the controls around it.
In a survey of 3,235 respondents across 24 countries, 74% expect at least moderate agent use by 2027, while only 21% report mature governance for agentic AI (Deloitte, State of AI in the Enterprise, 2026). The gap shows up at launch: a well-written system prompt and the hope that the model behaves.
Risk leads and platform engineers face two bad options. Block launch until a full governance program exists, and the business routes around you with unmanaged tools. Wave it through with a policy document, and the first incident becomes your governance program.
The answer is a short, fixed set of runtime guardrails that ship with the first production request, each with an owner and a metric. Seven is enough. This is not about data residency or sector regulation; it is about what runs in the request path, every time.
If a launch date is already on the calendar, check your request path for missing guardrails with the team.
Governance on paper does not run in the request path. Guardrails do.
Read these as a pipeline, not a list of policies: each sits at a specific point between the user and the response.
1. Input filtering. Screen the prompt before the model sees it: jailbreak attempts, prompt injection carried in documents or web pages, and requests far outside the application's purpose. A topic allowlist ("this assistant answers billing questions") catches more real misuse than a long blocklist.
2. Output moderation. Check what the model produces before the user or a downstream system sees it. For streamed responses, check as tokens arrive rather than after the full answer, or the user reads the problem before you catch it.
3. PII handling. Detect and mask personal data on the way in, and check for it on the way out. Redact before the model, before tools, and before logs: the log is the copy most teams forget.
4. Tool permissioning. Give an agent the least privilege its task needs. Separate read tools from write tools, allowlist the systems it can call, and require approval for any action that moves money, sends external messages or deletes records.
5. Spend caps and rate limits. Cap tokens per request, per user and per day, and cap the number of steps an agent can t

items.title: Expanding our partnership with GSA to bring Claude to all levels of government
items.detailText:
Anthropic is an AI safety and research company that's working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems.
We are expanding our partnership with the General Services Administration (GSA) through a new agreement that gives government partners a 40% discount on Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government, and the Claude API. For the first time, the discount applies across every product surface, including when agencies buy from us directly today and through cloud providers in the coming months. The discount also extends to state, local, tribal and territorial governments.
We are also launching a dedicated program to help agencies implement and make the most of their Claude use. These programs are commonly leveraged by our private sector customers and we’re looking forward to bringing those best practices to our public sector partners in the coming weeks.
The discounts offered through the agreement are estimated to save the government $1 billion. Agencies are not bound by a minimum spend commitment and will be able to pay for the usage they consume.
Government agencies are using Claude to solve some of their most important challenges. Examples include managing backlogs, records and forms, and modernizing old code. Some of the ways agencies are using Claude include:
Agencies can use Claude for their most sensitive unclassified work. Claude for Government, which delivers Claude's coding and agentic work capabilities and provides near-feature parity with commercial offerings at a FedRAMP High authorization level, was made generally available on September 30.
Agencies building their own tools can use Claude through Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud’s Vertex AI. On Bedrock, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High, with select models authorized for DoD IL4 and IL5 workloads in AWS GovCloud. On Vertex AI, Claude is authorized for FedRAMP High.
Claude Enterprise is in process for FedRAMP Moderate authorization through the FedRAMP 20x program, marking the next evolution of how we are bringing the same innovative technology available commercially to the government.
Government agencies can buy Claude at the OneGov discount through GSA's Multiple Award Schedule today. Whether your department or agency already uses Claude or is interested in using it, our Public Sector team will help discuss your options.
Anthropic is a Public Benefit Corporation. Our mission is the responsible development and maintenance of advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity.
